newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SWISS FRANCS, MARK FIRMS IN ACTIVE TRADE ON BCE.
newsitem.headline: SWISS FRANCS, MARK FIRMS IN ACTIVE TRADE ON BCE.

text.p: Yen futures soared while Swiss franc futures were the most actively traded contracts on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday, one of the year's most active days with a turnover of 9.84 billion forints.

Swiss franc futures, closed higher for all maturities, but March 1998 was the most actively traded instrument with 6,000 contracts, with its settlement price finishing at 143.80 forints, up 30 fillers.
"The Swiss francs have been strengthening since April... uncertainties over the EMU made the Swiss francs firmer against the mark," said BCE trader Janos Szolyka of Swap.
Good macroeconomic figures in Switzerland also made it stronger and futures prices on the BCE reflect this, he said.
Yen futures settled higher by between 3.72 and 5.62 forints for 100 yen, exceeding the three forint limit after which intraday clearing is ordered.
"The yen's rise stems from the fact that the Japanese finance ministry began a campaign for a stronger yen and a weaker dollar," Szolyka said. "These verbal interventions made markets uncertain."
Yen sellers tried to close their positions and began to buy, driving prices higher, he said.
The dollar eased and the pound closed weaker for all months, while the Ecu was stable.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange mark and dollar futures traded, with lower dollar settlement prices for all maturities and steady to higher prices for the mark.
